An append-only log requires the write operation to be idempotent to handle at-least-once delivery, though the writer merely needs to retry, because appending modifies state (so it's not safe) but must result in exactly one append.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the event ID is not deterministically generated by the writer, retrying will produce different IDs and violate idempotency.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"At-least-once delivery guarantees retries. The append operation mutates the log, so it is not a safe operation. For replay to be deterministic, the log must apply an idempotent operation: if the event ID exists, do nothing; else append. This makes the log's append method idempotent rather than requiring the client's broader state changes to be inherently idempotent.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
